prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (alias/call sign Juniper) provides 24/7 intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, regional coordination, and shared operational picture for emergency medical requests across participating jurisdictions. Mandate: translate reported emergencies into prioritized incidents and coordinate appropriate response under approved clinical and jurisdictional protocols. It maintains knowledge of incidents, available units, assignments, regional resource status, vehicle serviceability, maintenance/access constraints. Participating jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy responsibility; regional service coordinates agreed response activity. Operating area is divided into response zones reflecting distance, road access, ambulance capacity; zone boundaries are maintained with jurisdictions and reviewed when road networks, population patterns, or agreements change.

Actors/elements: Call Taker Mara enters request via Computer Aided Dispatch Console. Triage Supervisor assigns/confirms priority and directs extra clinical review. Regional Medical Director owns clinical triage policy/limits. Dispatch personnel apply protocols; seek clinical guidance beyond authority; consider travel time, road restrictions, weather, closures for routing/ETA. Shift Commander (call sign Sundial) is on-duty operational authority for coordination/continuity; sets surge priorities; escalates beyond center authority; does not supersede clinical-policy authority or scene clinical judgment. Radio Coordinator (call sign Mistral) manages/monitors Regional Radio Network, maintains clear communications, confirms assigned channels and backup procedures at shift start; radio checks verify weak-signal coverage and issues. Fleet Maintenance Cell (call sign Bluejay) provides awareness of vehicle serviceability/maintenance constraints; monitors vehicle availability, scheduled servicing, defects reducing zone coverage; produces Battery Swap Voucher for authorized battery replacement. Data Quality Officer reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, compliance with information-handling rules. Ambulance Coordination Platform supports incident/unit/resource view. Paramedic Crew handles scene patient assessment/care. Ambulance Unit 417 may be assigned. Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates receiving capacity/destination constraints. Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center are destinations; each zone has primary/alternate routes to them, subject to clinical direction/current access.

North Gate Status Board presents northern access/queue conditions and produces North Approach Queue Snapshot. South Gate Status Board presents southern access incl. ambulance-entry restrictions. Both checked at shift start and on relevant access changes. Crews verify constrained routes before committing. Readiness checks confirm ambulance staffing, communications, supplies, fuel, condition, maintenance restrictions.

New part:
S044: The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
S045: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
S046: The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
S047: The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
S048: The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
S049: The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
S050: Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
S051: The Regional Dispatch Center handles incoming emergency calls through a controlled intake process that creates an incident record for coordination.
S052: Call Taker Mara is also known by the radio alias Larkspur.
S053: The Hospital Liaison Desk is also known by the coordination alias Kestrel.
S054: Call Taker Mara establishes the caller's location before collecting medical details.
S055: Call Taker Mara asks for the street address, municipality, and any building, floor, or entrance information needed to find the patient.
S056: Call Taker Mara confirms the location by repeating the address and checking it against the caller's description of nearby landmarks.
S057: Call Taker Mara asks whether the caller can provide a callback number in case the connection is lost.
S058: Call Taker Mara gathers the patient's age, level of consciousness, breathing status, and the main reason emergency help is needed.
S059: Call Taker Mara uses direct questions to distinguish observed symptoms from information reported by someone else.
S060: Call Taker Mara records the time symptoms began when the caller can provide a reliable estimate.
S061: Call Taker Mara notes access barriers such as locked entrances, restricted roads, or difficulty reaching the patient.
S062: Call Taker Mara produces the Caller Location Correction Slip when the caller's address needs documented clarification.
S063: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks entered location details against available address and map data.
S064: If the location does not resolve cleanly, Call Taker Mara asks focused follow-up questions and updates the incident record.
S065: Call Taker Mara remains engaged with the caller when further information could change the response priority or access plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
